title: Stretch your dollar at the Nintendo eShop with this deal from Newegg
summary: Newegg is offering a one-day promotion: $5 off every $50 Nintendo eShop gift card (use promo code SSERA438), limited to purchases up to $250. eShop funds can be used on games, Nintendo Switch Game Vouchers and Switch Online/Expansion Pass subscriptions. Some new Switch 2 titles are excluded.
content:
Digital currency in the Nintendo eShop can be applied towards game vouchers or titles for the Switch.

New games for the Nintendo Switch 2 can cost as much as $79.99, and some accessories can cost up to $119.99. But you can always count on friends at Newegg to help take the edge off with a deal that’ll save you some money at the Nintendo eShop. For today only, you can save $5 on every $50 gift card purchase for the Nintendo eShop. This promotion is valid for today only and is limited to purchases of $250 or less, but it’s an easy way to get a little extra bang for your buck. Just use the promo code SSERA438 at checkout to knock $5 off every $50 gift card purchase. As one review for this product states, the only downside to this deal is that it “Does not include a small Charles Martinet to make \"Wahoo\" noises when you redeem it.”

$45 at Newegg ($50)

While you can always spend your new balance on games, funds for the Nintendo eShop can also be applied to Nintendo Switch Game Vouchers. These $99.98 coupons can be redeemed for two eligible first-party Nintendo titles, which typically cost $59.99 each, saving you a cool $20 if you play your cards right. Unfortunately, this won’t include new titles for the Nintendo Switch 2, like Mario Kart World or Donkey Kong Bananza.

Nintendo eShop funds can also be used to purchase Nintendo Switch Online or Expansion Pass subscriptions, which not only allows you to save your Switch data in cloud, you’ll also get access to a growing library of classic Nintendo titles for the NES, SNES, N64, Game Boy, and Game Boy Advance. Nintendo also recently announced that it will be adding a collection of classic games from the Nintendo GameCube to the Expansion Pass library, which will be playable exclusively on the Switch 2.
